$comment: Written by `agentic-factory init`. Every project-specific value lives here; the handbooks, templates and scripts read it. Never put secrets in this file.

rhythm.$modes: day-plan-night-build: the human plans, tests and decides by day, the Controller builds unattended at night, morning handover; continuous: the Controller builds whenever signed-off work exists and asks as questions arise; custom: quietHours define when the Controller may start new work

steering.$modes: github-issues: tickets are GitHub issues with labels; orca-tasks: tickets are docs/tasks/T<n>-*.md files

hosts.$comment: A remote server is an option, not a must. The controller runs on one host (the local machine or a remote one). Workers run on zero or more hosts; each has its own paths, Orca environment and capacity. With no remote hosts everything runs locally.

controller.$wake: idleMinutes: an idle project (no new inbox line, worker message or finished wave, no ready ticket, no running worker) is woken at most this often. busyPointerMinutes: a Controller that Orca reads as busy gets a one-line pointer to what is waiting after this long. dialogPatterns: regular expressions (case-insensitive, per line) matched against the last 8 lines of the Controller's screen; while one matches, nothing is typed (Enter would take the default). After dialogHoldMinutes the Front agent is told that the Controller seems to wait at a dialog, once and again only when the question changes. The values shown are the defaults.
controller.$hung: A Controller that is busy, whose terminal keeps changing, and whose status.md and journal did not change for 'minutes' is reported to the Front agent. restart: only true lets the heartbeat restart it (once, after 'restartAfterMinutes', if its terminal shows the same frame twice and no wave, gate or push runs); the default false reports only. patterns: regular expressions that, visible for patternMinutes, also count as hung (report only); none are shipped. resetAfterDays: a restart this long ago no longer counts as 'restarted once'.
controller.$restart: contextPercent: the Controller starts itself fresh (restart.mjs) after a wave or when idle once its context use is above this share. contextGapMinutes / minGapMinutes: restart.mjs refuses a restart sooner than this after the last (asked by the Controller / any other). afterGateMinutes: no restart this soon after a gate, wave or push.

frontAgent.$kind: terminal (default): the Front agent is an agent session in a terminal, woken by statuswatch.mjs; orca-bot: an Orca bot on this machine is the Front agent, woken by one Orca automation with a precheck (botwatch.mjs). One bot can serve several projects: name the same bot in each.
frontAgent.$bot: orca-bot only: the bot's name as `orca bot list` shows it. Create the bot in Orca first; start creates its watch automation.
frontAgent.$staleMinutes: orca-bot only: the bot's watch wakes it once when the Controller's status.md gets older than this.

agents.$runners: orca: workers run in Orca worktrees and terminals; terminal: workers run as plain codex/claude/pi processes in git worktrees
agents.$piRoleModels: Optional, e.g. { "Developer": "provider/model-id" }: a Pi worker of a listed role starts pinned to that provider/model instead of its tier's model. Other roles and other agents keep their tier. An explicit --model still wins.
agents.$calibration: The model names are examples of what the agent CLI offers; init asks for the available ones. auto: calibrate-models.mjs moves a role one tier down when its pass rate is high and rounds are low, one tier up when failures cluster; manual: it only recommends.

capacity.$comment: Defaults for every worker host; a host's own capacity block overrides single values.

calibration.$comment: The caps above are starting values. auto: start low (startSuite), raise by step while the host stays quiet for raiseAfterQuietMinutes at the cap, lower on pressure or load timeouts; the audit verifies. manual: use the configured caps as they are.

commands.$docsChecks: Optional. formatCheck (e.g. a formatter's check mode such as "prettier --check .", run through the project's own tooling) and markdownCheck (e.g. "markdownlint-cli2 '**/*.md'") are what a documentation-only wave runs instead of verify and e2e (docsOnly.enabled); an empty one is skipped.
commands.$formatStaged: Optional, off when empty: pre-commit runs this formatter in write mode on the staged files (paths appended) and stages the result, e.g. "prettier --write --ignore-unknown" run through the project's own tooling. Or { "command": "…", "paths": ["**/*.py"] } to pass only matching files. Partially staged files keep their unstaged changes.

docsOnly.$enabled: true: a change that touches documentation only (tools/factory-guardrails.mjs docs-only, fail closed) gets no Tester (the ticket's own spec review and report, new files, do not count against it); a wave with nothing but documentation runs commands.formatCheck and commands.markdownCheck instead of the full gates (with neither configured, or with the task's process files or a status branch in the wave, the full gates). Read from the main branch's factory.config.json, so it takes a reviewed change to get it there (agentic-factory init asks once; later it is a ticket: docs/testing.md). false: every change takes the full path.
docsOnly.$paths: Where documentation lives (** any depth, * and ? within a directory, {a,b}); each pattern starts with a directory name or names top-level files. Only plain Markdown and raster images count; the files the factory installs or reads as process state (protocols, coordinator and workflow docs, reviews, tickets), agent instruction files, dot paths and executable files never do. Read from the main branch: a change cannot widen its own allowlist.
docsOnly.$extraTypes: Opt-in file types that can carry code: "svg", "mdx". Empty: Markdown and raster images only.

cleanup.$pendingWarnMinutes: How long removable work may wait before status and doctor report it. cleanup.mjs deletes only with --apply; a run without it records since when something waited (cleanup-pending.json in the Controller directory), and a run with --apply clears that. Default 30.
